planets.name: KELT-1 b
planets.description: Transiting planet of KELT-1 with a 1.22-day year, found in 2012.

text.card: KELT-1 b was found in 2012 by KELT as it crossed its star.
text.introduction: It is the only planet known around KELT-1. Its orbit and size follow Siverd et al. 2012's fit, the archive's default.
text.locator: NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table, default parameter set (pl_refname SIVERD_ET_AL__2012): disc_year 2012, disc_facility KELT, sy_pnum 1; pl_orbper 1.2174936, pl_radj 1.11, pl_bmassj 27.23

thermal.source: Deming et al. 2023, dayside brightness temperature at 3.6 µm (uniform reanalysis of Spitzer's eclipses, CDS J/AJ/165/104 table 2)
thermal.chosen: 2 measured of 2 rows; the smallest relative uncertainty, then the longest wavelength

phaseCurves.label: Spitzer
phaseCurves.observed: a Spitzer IRAC 4.5 µm phase curve (program 11095, first published by Beatty et al. (2019))

record.source: Bell et al. (2021), MNRAS 504, 3316, 'A comprehensive reanalysis of Spitzer's 4.5 um phase curves, and the phase variations of the ultra-hot Jupiters MASCARA-1b and KELT-16b' (doi:10.1093/mnras/stab1027; arXiv:2010.00687). Spitzer IRAC 4.5 um phase curve of KELT-1b, program 11095, first published by Beatty et al. (2019) and reanalysed here. Values read from the authors' LaTeX source: the table of preferred SPCA model parameters (tab:preferred), row KELT-1b, detector model BLISS. The preferred fit is first order (the caption of its figure names the mode BLISS_v1 with PSF centroiding), so the printed semi-amplitude and offset are the whole phase variation (section 4.1: semi-amplitude sqrt(C1^2 + D1^2), offset east -arctan2(D1, C1)). The figure's file name carries no PSFX suffix and section 6.2 says the comparison keeps the FWM-centroiding fits, so the text does not settle which centroiding the table row used; either way the fit is BLISS, first order.

model.equation: F_p = F_day [1 + C1 (cos psi - 1) + D1 sin psi], psi counted from mid-eclipse (section 4.1), printed as its semi-amplitude and the offset east of its maximum.
